blocks.content: WORKDIR sets the working directory for every instruction that follows it in the Dockerfile, and for the container's process once it starts.
Once declared, WORKDIR /app means every subsequent RUN, CMD, COPY, and ADD instruction operates relative to /app, instead of needing an absolute path spelled out every single time.

blocks.alt: Sets the base directory for everything that follows

blocks.content:
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .          # copies into /app
RUN npm install   # runs inside /app
CMD ["node", "index.js"]   # also runs from /app

blocks.content: 2. It Affects the Running Container Too
blocks.text: 2. It Affects the Running Container Too

blocks.content: It is not just a build-time convenience, the working directory WORKDIR sets is also where the container's main process starts from at runtime, exactly as if you had cd'd there before launching it.

blocks.alt: It shapes both the build and the running container

blocks.content: 3. It Creates the Directory If Needed
blocks.text: 3. It Creates the Directory If Needed

blocks.content: Unlike a plain shell cd, which fails on a nonexistent directory, WORKDIR creates the directory automatically if it does not already exist, one less step to remember.

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: WORKDIR sets the base directory for every following instruction, and for the container's process once it actually starts.
It creates the target directory automatically if it does not exist, unlike a plain shell cd.
